findings.observation: The site plan includes a Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing electrical infrastructure routing, transformers, and meters. The Master Comment Report includes an Electric Review section indicating Austin Energy has completed a completeness check. However, no Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form was located in the submitted supplementary documents, project review form, or consolidated site plan application. The completeness check merely notes 'EL 1. AE completeness check complete' without specifying which forms were submitted.
findings.reasoning: An ESPA form is required to initiate electric service design and determine transformer/service requirements. The presence of preliminary electrical design does not confirm that an ESPA form was submitted to Austin Energy to formally initiate the service request process. The project may have proceeded with design planning before or instead of submitting the ESPA. Without evidence of ESPA submission (either in the submitted documents or in correspondence confirming its receipt by AE), the requirement cannot be verified as satisfied.
findings.comment: Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form submission to Austin Energy not verified in submitted documentation. Provide evidence of ESPA submission to AE or confirm whether a service-only determination has been made that waives the ESPA requirement.

findings.observation: A Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is present in the site plan submission showing electrical infrastructure. Austin Energy completed a completeness check per the completeness check results. However, no signed AE Submittal Form was located in the supplementary documents, project review form, or consolidated site plan application package.
findings.reasoning: The AE Submittal Form is a required standard form for all sites undergoing land development review requiring Austin Energy coordination. While a completeness check was completed, the specific AE Submittal Form (a signed authorization form for AE to participate in land development review) is not documented in the submittal. The completeness check status does not confirm that the signed form has been submitted.
findings.comment: Signed AE Submittal Form not verified in submitted documentation. Provide the signed AE Submittal Form required for land development review coordination with Austin Energy.

findings.observation: A Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is present in the site plan submission. Austin Energy completed a completeness check per the completeness check results. However, no signed AE Standard Notes Form was located in the supplementary documents, project review form, or consolidated site plan application package.
findings.reasoning: The AE Standard Notes Form is a required standard form for all sites undergoing land development review requiring Austin Energy coordination. While a completeness check was completed, the specific AE Standard Notes Form (a required signed form acknowledging AE standard requirements and conditions) is not documented in the submittal. The completeness check status does not confirm that this signed form has been submitted.
findings.comment: Signed AE Standard Notes Form not verified in submitted documentation. Provide the signed AE Standard Notes Form required for land development review coordination with Austin Energy.

findings.observation: A Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is part of the submitted site plan. However, no documentation confirms that a full-scale copy of the entire 39-sheet site plan was specifically provided to Austin Energy for their review and approval as required by UCM § 1.16.0. The Master Comment Report references AE site comments in an external Bluebeam link, but submission of a full-scale site plan copy to AE is not explicitly documented.
findings.reasoning: Applicants must provide a full-scale copy of the entire site plan to AE Design as part of the standard submission requirements. While the site plan exists and AE has reviewed it (per the Master Comment Report), the specific action of providing AE with a full-scale site plan copy is not documented in the submitted records. The external Bluebeam link suggests AE has reviewed the plans, but does not confirm that a full-scale copy meeting specification requirements was provided.
findings.comment: Full-scale copy of entire site plan submission to Austin Energy not verified. Provide documentation or correspondence confirming that a complete, full-scale copy of all 39 site plan sheets was submitted to Austin Energy Design for their review.

findings.observation: The site plan includes a Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and general notes (Sheet 3) with electric transmission requirements. However, after review of Sheet 21 blocks and guides, Sheet 3 electric notes, the Engineer's Summary Letter, and all supplementary documents, no electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis documents were located in the submittal. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows routing and equipment placement but does not include load calculations or capacity analysis documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that electrical load calculations, demand projections, and capacity analysis be provided to AE Design. These are essential technical documents needed for AE to evaluate whether existing service is adequate or whether upgrades are required. The absence of these calculations from the submitted documents represents a gap in required electrical design documentation. Load calculations are typically the basis for determining transformer size, service requirements, and capacity adequacy.
findings.comment: Electrical load calculations, demand projections, and capacity analysis not provided to Austin Energy Design. Provide detailed electrical load calculations showing peak demand projections and capacity analysis for the proposed 39-unit development to AE Design for review and approval.

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows general routing of electrical infrastructure, transformers, and meters but does not include voltage and service size specifications documented in the plan notes or blocks. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 provides utility notes about water and wastewater (HDPE and PVC specifications) but does not document electrical service voltage (e.g., 120/240V, 277/480V, 12.47kV) or service size (e.g., 200A, 400A, transformer capacity in kVA). No voltage and service size specifications were found in supplementary documents or correspondence.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that voltage and service size specifications required for service be provided to AE Design. This is a fundamental technical specification that AE Design must evaluate and approve. Service voltage and size determinations cannot be made by the applicant; they must be determined and approved by AE Design based on the calculated load and available infrastructure. The absence of these specifications, or their specification without AE Design approval, is a deficiency.
findings.comment: Voltage and service size specifications not documented on site plan or provided to Austin Energy Design. Provide specifications for service voltage (e.g., 120/240V or three-phase voltage) and service size (e.g., amperage and transformer kVA ratings) to AE Design and document AE Design approval on site plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) provides a detailed Site Data Table (Block 16) that includes site area (94,192 sf / 2.162 acres), gross floor area by building type, building coverage, and impervious cover percentages. However, the total Gross Floor Area for the entire project is not explicitly stated as a single summary value on the site plan sheets or in the general notes. The Site Data Table on Sheet 9 shows individual building GFA values, and the guide indicates a total of 83,986 sf, but this is not clearly labeled as 'Total GFA' on the plan itself in a prominent location for AE system grid load monitoring purposes.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that total Gross Floor Area (GFA) in square feet be provided on the site plan for AE system grid load monitoring. This is a standard requirement for AE to assess system capacity and loading. While GFA data exists in the project documentation (83,986 sf total), if it is not prominently displayed on the site plan sheets themselves (as opposed to supplementary documents), this represents a documentation deficiency on the plans. AE reviewers expect to see total GFA clearly labeled on site plan cover sheets or plan sheets for easy reference.
findings.comment: Total Gross Floor Area (GFA) not prominently displayed on site plan for Austin Energy system grid load monitoring. Add total project GFA (83,986 sq ft) to the site plan cover sheet or main site plan sheet in a prominent location visible to AE reviewers.

findings.observation: The Master Comment Report includes an Electric Review section indicating that Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements. This suggests some level of AE Design coordination. However, no formal correspondence or proof of AE Design approval of the preliminary electric design was located in the supplementary documents package. The review comments exist in an external Bluebeam link (which is not accessible in the submitted documentation), and the completeness check confirms AE completed their review, but specific design approval letters or correspondence confirming acceptance of the preliminary design are not documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electric design. This is a standard requirement when AE Design coordination is needed for infrastructure work, pole relocation, or facility modifications. The Master Comment Report suggests design coordination occurred, but the specific correspondence documenting design approval is not provided in the submittal. Completeness check completion does not constitute design approval—it is merely an administrative confirmation that AE reviewed the application.
findings.comment: Proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electric design not provided. Provide copies of all email or letter correspondence with AE Design confirming approval of the preliminary electrical design plan.

findings.observation: Austin Energy has completed a completeness check (per Completeness Check Results), indicating some level of service coordination. However, no letter from Austin Energy stating that utility service can be provided to the site or identifying necessary easements or service upgrades was located in the supplementary documents. No formal AE Service Verification Letter or service availability letter was found in the submitted documentation.
findings.reasoning: A letter from Austin Energy confirming that service can be provided and identifying any necessary easements or required service upgrades is a standard requirement for land development review. This letter typically comes from AE's Service Availability or Design department and confirms that electric service is feasible. The completeness check completion alone does not provide this specific confirmation. Without this letter, there is no documented verification that AE has confirmed service availability.
findings.comment: Letter from Austin Energy confirming service availability and identifying necessary easements or service upgrades not provided. Provide a letter from Austin Energy stating that utility service can be provided to the site and identifying any required service upgrades, easements, or facility modifications.

findings.observation: The project was submitted by an applicant, but after review of the supplementary documents (Consolidated Site Plan Application, Project Review Form, and other submissions), no specific Authorization Letter or Owner Authorization Letter explicitly stating 'Austin Energy' and authorizing AE to participate in land development review was located. The Consolidated Site Plan Application includes a Contacts and Authorizations section, but the specific language required (explicit mention of 'Austin Energy') in the authorization is not documented in the materials reviewed.
findings.reasoning: When agents or entities other than the property owner submit on behalf of the owner, UCM § 1.16.0 requires specific authorization. An Agent Authorization Letter or Owner Authorization Letter that explicitly states 'Austin Energy' is required to demonstrate that the agent or owner has authorized Austin Energy's involvement in the project review. The absence of this specific authorization document is a deficiency, particularly when the agent is coordinating with multiple departments (AE being one of them).
findings.comment: Agent Authorization Letter or Owner Authorization Letter explicitly stating 'Austin Energy' not provided. Provide written authorization from the property owner (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC) or agent explicitly authorizing Austin Energy to participate in land development review and coordination.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents 16 notes about electric transmission lines and easements, confirming that transmission facilities (≥60kV) are present on or near the property. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical infrastructure routing. However, no evidence of CAD files submitted specifically to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for review was located in the supplementary documents or correspondence. The site plan shows transmission easement requirements but does not document that AutoCAD files were provided to AE Transmission Engineering.
findings.reasoning: When a project involves or is near AE transmission lines (≥60kV facilities), CAD files must be submitted to AE Transmission Engineering for specialized review per UCM § 1.16.0(1). The presence of transmission easement notes on Sheet 3 confirms that transmission facilities are relevant to this project. The lack of documented submission of CAD files to AE Transmission Engineering represents a gap. AutoCAD drawings must be submitted in version 2016 or newer and include all relevant infrastructure crossing or near transmission lines.
findings.comment: CAD files for Austin Energy Transmission Engineering review not verified as submitted. Provide evidence that AutoCAD files (version 2016 or newer) have been submitted to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for review of infrastructure near transmission facilities.

findings.observation: The site plan includes a Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing electrical infrastructure. However, no documentation confirms the AutoCAD version of the files (if any CAD files were provided). The site plan sheets themselves appear to be in a PDF or image format, and no specific AutoCAD file version metadata or submission documentation was located indicating that AutoCAD drawings in version 2016 or newer were submitted to Austin Energy.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that AutoCAD drawings submitted to Austin Energy be in version 2016 or newer format. This is a technical specification for electronic submissions. Without evidence of the AutoCAD file version being submitted or documentation of file version metadata, it cannot be verified that this requirement has been met. The mere existence of site plan drawings does not confirm they meet the AutoCAD version specification.
findings.comment: AutoCAD drawings not verified as submitted in version 2016 or newer. Provide AutoCAD drawing files (version 2016 or newer) to Austin Energy in electronic format for transmission engineering review, or provide documentation confirming the AutoCAD version of files already submitted.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents extensive transmission line easement requirements (16 notes), confirming that transmission facilities (≥60kV) are on the property. However, no documentation confirms that AutoCAD drawings showing the electrical design and site infrastructure have been submitted to the Austin Energy reviewer for transmission line review. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan exists but submission of the AutoCAD version to AE reviewers is not verified.
findings.reasoning: When a project involves transmission lines (≥60kV facilities) or development is within 100 feet of transmission line wires, AutoCAD drawings must be submitted to the Austin Energy reviewer for transmission line review per UCM § 1.16.0(1). The presence of transmission easement notes confirms transmission facilities are relevant. The absence of documented submission of AutoCAD drawings to AE Transmission Engineering represents a deficiency in the submission requirements.
findings.comment: AutoCAD drawings not verified as submitted to Austin Energy reviewer for transmission line review. Submit all electrical and site design drawings in AutoCAD format (version 2016 or newer) to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for review of infrastructure near transmission facilities.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement requirements, indicating transmission facilities are present on the site. However, examination of the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Site Plan (Sheet 9), and other sheets does not reveal clear documentation showing that any proposed infrastructure crosses Austin Energy transmission lines. Sheet 21 shows electrical equipment placement but does not document transmission line crossing conditions. No profile design showing crossing infrastructure clearances was located.
findings.reasoning: If proposed infrastructure (such as building improvements, utility lines, or site infrastructure) crosses Austin Energy transmission lines, a profile design showing the crossing and required clearances must be provided in AutoCAD drawings per UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv). The project documentation does not clearly indicate whether any proposed infrastructure actually crosses transmission lines or if the transmission lines run adjacently to the development area. If crossing conditions exist, the profile design documentation would be missing. If crossing does not occur, this item may not be applicable.
findings.comment: Profile design of crossing infrastructure not verified. If any proposed infrastructure crosses Austin Energy transmission lines, provide profile views in AutoCAD format showing the crossing and demonstrating compliance with required clearances.

findings.observation: The site plan includes a Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing proposed electrical infrastructure layout. However, no separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan with detailed electrical design showing plan and profile views was located in the supplementary documents or as part of the submitted site plan sheets. The preliminary design is shown on the site plan itself, but a separate, dedicated AE Distribution Plan document is not evidenced in the submission.
findings.reasoning: When modifications to existing AE facilities are proposed, a separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views is required per UCM § 1.16.0(1). This is a formal document prepared by or in coordination with AE Design. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan on Sheet 21 shows the applicant's proposed routing and equipment, but this may not meet the requirement for a formal AE Distribution Plan if modifications to existing AE facilities are involved. Without documentation of existing AE facility modifications required, the necessity of this item depends on the scope of work affecting existing AE infrastructure.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Distribution Plan not verified as submitted. If modifications to existing Austin Energy facilities are proposed, provide a separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views.

findings.observation: The site plan includes drainage features (biofiltration-detention pond shown on Sheets 15, 16) and electrical facilities (shown on Sheet 21). Sheet 21 shows electrical routing and infrastructure. However, profile plans specifically showing electrical facilities with required clearances when electrical facilities interact with drainage features (such as the biofiltration-detention pond) are not explicitly documented in the reviewed materials. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows plan view routing but does not include detailed profile views showing vertical clearances from the pond.
findings.reasoning: When electrical facilities interact with drainage features such as retention ponds or detention ponds, profile plans showing the electrical facilities and required clearances must be submitted per UCM § 1.10.7 and UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv). These profiles demonstrate compliance with safety clearance requirements and proper drainage/electrical separation. The absence of specific profile documentation showing vertical clearances between electrical equipment and the biofiltration-detention pond represents a potential gap in required design documentation.
findings.comment: Profile plans not provided showing electrical facilities with required clearances from drainage features. Provide profile views showing the biofiltration-detention pond and nearby electrical facilities (transformers, lines, pull boxes) with dimensions demonstrating required vertical and horizontal clearances per UCM § 1.10.7.

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electrical routing and equipment placement, which may indicate conversion from overhead to underground service. However, no Austin Energy approved detail showing the specific design of overhead to underground conversion was located in the supplementary documents or site plan sheets. If conversion from overhead to underground is proposed, the specific conversion detail must be provided.
findings.reasoning: When converting existing overhead electric service to underground, an Austin Energy approved detail for the conversion must be provided per UCM § 1.3.13. This is an excess facilities item that requires AE design and approval. The detail specifies how the existing overhead service will be terminated and converted to underground service, including meter pedestal design, service entry, and related specifications. The absence of this specific detail, if overhead-to-underground conversion is part of the project scope, represents a deficiency.
findings.comment: Austin Energy approved detail for overhead to underground conversion not provided. If converting existing overhead electric service to underground, provide the Austin Energy approved conversion detail showing meter pedestal, service entry, and all related specifications.

applicableAreas: drainage pond and electrical utility areas
findings.observation: The site plan includes a biofiltration-detention pond in the northeast corner of the site (Sheets 15, 16) and electrical routing shown on Sheet 21. Review of the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) blocks and guide does not clearly indicate whether electric service trenching crosses under the detention pond or whether such routing passes under retention features. If underground electric service trenching is routed to pass under the detention pond, Austin Energy approval would be required.
findings.reasoning: When electric service trenching is routed to pass under detention ponds, approval from Austin Energy Design must be obtained per UCM § 1.10.7. This is because utility routing under storage features requires specific design considerations and AE coordination. Without clear documentation of the underground service routing relative to the pond location, or without evidence of AE approval if such routing exists, this requirement cannot be verified as met.
findings.comment: Austin Energy approval for underground electric service trenching under detention pond not verified. Confirm the route of underground electric service trenching relative to the biofiltration-detention pond. If the trenching passes under the pond, provide approval from Austin Energy Design for this routing.

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformers and electrical equipment routing but does not specifically indicate whether switchgear is required or shown on the plans. No load calculations or correspondence indicating switchgear requirement was found in the documentation. Switchgear is typically required only for very high loads (generally >1000 kVA or complex multi-service installations), which may not apply to this 39-unit residential development.
findings.reasoning: Switchgear installation requires coordination with Austin Energy design lead only when high electrical loads require switchgear per UCM § 1.16.0(6). For a 39-unit townhome project, switchgear is likely not required (typical residential loads are served by standard service transformers and panels). However, without load calculations showing the total project demand, the applicability of this requirement cannot be definitively determined. If load calculations show switchgear is not needed, this item would be n/a.
findings.comment: Switchgear applicability to this project not verified. Provide load calculations confirming whether switchgear is required. If switchgear is needed, provide evidence of coordination with Austin Energy Design lead.

applicableAreas: transformer pad locations on site plan
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pads located on the site plan (transformer symbols and locations are indicated). However, no documentation or correspondence confirming that pad-mounted transformer installation has been coordinated with Austin Energy Design lead was located. The block content for Sheet 21 does not mention transformer coordination or approval.
findings.reasoning: When new buildings increase load and require pad-mounted transformers, the installation must be coordinated with Austin Energy Design lead per UCM § 1.16.0(6). This is required to ensure proper siting, sizing, and connection to AE infrastructure. The presence of transformers on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan suggests they are part of the project design, but coordination with AE Design (beyond the general completeness check) is not documented. Evidence of this specific coordination should be provided.
findings.comment: Pad-mounted transformer coordination with Austin Energy Design lead not verified. Provide documentation or correspondence confirming that transformer locations and specifications have been coordinated with and approved by Austin Energy Design lead.

findings.observation: The site plan shows new electric service infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground routing on Sheet 21) for a new 39-unit development. This is a new site requiring electric service extension. However, no documentation confirming developer financial responsibility for line extension costs was located. The facts.md does not mention existing electric service at the site, and the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows new infrastructure routing, suggesting line extension is required. No cost responsibility acknowledgment or work order from Austin Energy indicating line extension fees was found.
findings.reasoning: When line extension is required to provide electric service to a site, the developer must acknowledge financial responsibility for line extension costs per UCM § 1.3.12 (the AE Line Extension Policy). The project shows new electric service infrastructure, which strongly suggests line extension is necessary. Without documentation of cost responsibility acknowledgment or AE correspondence indicating whether line extension is required and who is responsible, this requirement cannot be verified as met. A formal acknowledgment of line extension cost responsibility may be required before site plan approval.
findings.comment: Developer financial responsibility for line extension not documented. Provide documentation from Austin Energy indicating whether line extension to the site is required and acknowledge developer responsibility for all line extension costs per UCM § 1.3.12.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement requirements and notes that existing electric transmission facilities are on or near the property. However, no documentation confirms whether existing AE facilities must be relocated or removed as part of the development. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed new infrastructure routing but does not document conflicts with existing AE facilities or required relocations. No cost responsibility acknowledgment for facility relocation was located.
findings.reasoning: When existing AE facilities must be relocated or removed, developer financial responsibility must be acknowledged prior to site plan approval per UCM § 1.3.13 (Excess Facilities/Excess Cost Policy). Without documentation of existing facility conflicts, relocation requirements, or cost responsibility, the applicability of this item cannot be fully determined. If facility relocation is required, the acknowledgment document is missing.
findings.comment: Developer financial responsibility for electric facility relocation or removal not documented. If existing Austin Energy facilities must be relocated or removed for the development, provide cost responsibility acknowledgment per UCM § 1.3.13 and documentation from Austin Energy indicating relocation scope and costs.

findings.observation: No documentation from Austin Energy indicating that system upgrades are required due to area grid overload, capacity limitations, or infrastructure improvements was located in the submitted documents. The facts.md and project documents do not reference any correspondence about substation capacity concerns or required system improvements. Austin Energy's completeness check is marked complete, but no specific indication of required system upgrades was noted.
findings.reasoning: When AE indicates that system upgrades (beyond standard line extension) are required due to grid overload or capacity limitations, developer financial responsibility must be acknowledged prior to site plan approval per UCM § 1.3.13. This typically comes from Austin Energy as a formal determination during the ESPA or service request process. Without such correspondence from AE, it cannot be determined if upgrades are required or if developer financial responsibility acknowledgment is needed.
findings.comment: No correspondence from Austin Energy identifying required system upgrades found. If Austin Energy has determined that electric system upgrades are required for this development, provide documentation and acknowledge developer financial responsibility for these costs per UCM § 1.3.13.

findings.observation: No documentation of Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee payment or receipt was located in the supplementary documents. The completeness check notes that AE completed their review, but no fee receipt or payment confirmation was provided. The Consolidated Site Plan Application does not reference fee payment documentation.
findings.reasoning: Austin Energy requires a Site Plan Review fee for all sites undergoing land development review requiring AE coordination. This is a standard administrative requirement. Without documentation of fee payment (receipt or invoice), the requirement cannot be verified as met. AE may not issue formal approval or permits until the fee is paid and documented.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee not documented. Provide proof of payment or fee receipt to Austin Energy for site plan review services.

findings.observation: Sheet 2 is the Subdivision Plat sheet. After review of the site plan sheets and supplementary documents, the plat content was not examined in detail for the presence of the eight required Austin Energy plat notes covering: (i) AE pruning/removal rights, (ii) easement and access provision, (iii) owner erosion control and tree protection responsibilities, (iv) clearance maintenance responsibility, and (v-viii) transmission easement restrictions if applicable. The facts.md references multiple easements on the property (some not yet depicted per the facts), and the plat would be the appropriate location for these notes.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires eight specific plat notes covering AE rights, responsibilities, and easement restrictions when a plat or easement documents are part of the land development submittal. The requirement specifically applies when plat documents are submitted. Given that this is a site plan with a recorded subdivision plat (Sheet 2) and multiple easements noted in the facts.md, the plat notes requirement likely applies. The absence of documented plat notes representing a deficiency in the site plan application.
findings.comment: Plat notes required per UCM § 1.16.0(8) not verified on Sheet 2. Add all eight required notes to the subdivision plat covering: (i) Austin Energy tree pruning and removal rights, (ii) easement and access provision for AE, (iii) owner erosion control and tree protection responsibilities near AE facilities, (iv) owner clearance maintenance responsibility, and (v-viii) transmission easement access, maintenance, and activity restrictions.

findings.observation: The facts.md notes transmission easement restrictions on the property. Sheet 31 is the Landscape Plan. However, without detailed examination of Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), the presence or absence of parkland designations overlapping with transmission easement areas cannot be definitively determined. The facts.md indicates transmission easement areas exist, but does not specifically indicate whether parkland is proposed within those areas. The plat designations would show any parkland areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(9) prohibits designation of land within transmission easements as parkland or for parkland dedication. If the project includes parkland dedication and any of the dedicated area overlaps with transmission easements, this is a deficiency. The review of available materials does not provide sufficient detail to confirm or deny parkland designation compliance. Additional examination of the plat and landscape plan would be needed.
findings.comment: Parkland designation within transmission easement areas not verified. Review Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) to confirm that no parkland is designated or proposed within transmission easement areas per UCM § 1.16.0(9).

findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission facilities on the property and includes note 2 requiring pre-construction safety meeting 48 hours before construction commences, and note 3 referencing Texas OSHA 20-foot clearance requirements. However, no formal documentation from the grading plan (Sheet 11) or supplementary documents confirming that Austin Energy was notified at least 48 hours prior to work near high-voltage lines and that satisfactory arrangements were made to de-energize, move, or relocate lines was found. The general notes include transmission requirements but do not include specific notification documentation.
findings.reasoning: Texas Health & Safety Code § 752.003 and UCM § 1.10.2(B) require documentation that Austin Energy was notified at least 48 hours prior to work near high-voltage lines and that satisfactory arrangements were made for de-energization or relocation. This is an ongoing requirement during construction, not a pre-approval item. The notes on Sheet 3 show the requirement is acknowledged, but actual notification and arrangement documentation would come later during construction. At the site plan review stage, this may not be fully verifiable, but the general acknowledgment of the requirement on the plans is appropriate.
findings.comment: Pre-construction notification arrangement with Austin Energy for work near high-voltage lines to be documented prior to construction. Ensure that before any construction or grading activity begins within 10 feet of overhead transmission lines, Austin Energy is notified at least 48 hours in advance per Texas Health & Safety Code § 752.003 and arrangements are made to de-energize or relocate lines.

applicableAreas: areas with existing or proposed AE primary voltage facilities
findings.observation: No survey showing proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities was located in the supplementary documents. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed electrical infrastructure but does not include proximity dimensions to existing AE primary voltage lines. No proximity survey document was found in the project files.
findings.reasoning: When AE Design requests a proximity survey (which is determined during the design coordination process), a survey must be provided showing distances from the customer's facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities per UCM § 1.10.3. This is typically required when development is within or near AE clearance zones. Without evidence of AE Design requesting this survey, or documentation providing it, the requirement status is unclear. The applicability depends on whether AE Design specifically requested a proximity survey.
findings.comment: Proximity survey not provided. If Austin Energy Design has requested a proximity survey showing distances between proposed facilities and existing AE primary voltage facilities, provide the survey documentation.

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical equipment (transformers, meters, pull boxes) and underground routing but does not include specific clearance dimensions or annotations demonstrating compliance with safety clearance standards. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 provides utility notes about water and wastewater specifications but does not reference electrical clearance dimensions. Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement clearance requirements (noting no digging within 25 feet, no trees within 25 feet, 20-foot clearance for equipment) but the site plan does not dimension these clearances for verification.
findings.reasoning: Plans must demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(2). This includes clearances per the National Electric Safety Code and City of Austin requirements. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows the general layout, specific clearance dimensions from buildings, drainage features, trees, and other structures are not annotated on the plan. This makes verification of clearance compliance impossible. Clearance dimensions must be shown on the plans with annotations confirming compliance.
findings.comment: Clearance dimensions for electric facilities not documented on plans. Add clearance dimensions to the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan showing that all proposed electrical facilities (transformers, conductors, meter pedestals, service lines) maintain required clearances from buildings, drainage features, trees, and other structures per UCM § 1.16.0(2) and National Electric Safety Code standards.

findings.observation: The facts.md documents multiple easements affecting the property, including electric easements. Sheet 2 is the Subdivision Plat which should show easement designations. However, review of the available documentation does not confirm that electric utility easements are clearly depicted with dimensions and labels on the plat, or that metes and bounds descriptions have been provided for any additional easements required by Austin Energy. The facts.md shows some easements are not depicted on the site plan and are missing from COA GIS layers.
findings.reasoning: Plans must demonstrate sufficient electric utility easements and provide metes and bounds descriptions for additional easements required by Austin Energy per UCM § 1.16.0(3). The facts.md specifically notes that some recorded easements are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan (Greenbelt and City of Austin Drainage easements). If electric easements are also not properly depicted or described, this represents a deficiency in demonstrating adequate easement areas and accessibility for AE operations and maintenance.
findings.comment: Electric utility easements not clearly demonstrated or described on site plan. Verify that all existing and required electric utility easements are properly depicted on Sheet 2 (Plat) with dimensions, and provide metes and bounds descriptions for any additional easements required by Austin Energy for service installation and ongoing maintenance.

applicableAreas: transmission easement and electrical facility access areas
findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement access requirements (notes 1, 8, 13 specifically address access and equipment access needs). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings, driveways, and site layout but does not explicitly demonstrate or annotate AE access routes for vehicles and equipment to reach transmission structures, poles, or other AE infrastructure. The presence of transmission structures and the layout shown do not clearly document maintained access routes for AE trucks and equipment.
findings.reasoning: Plans must demonstrate that development will maintain Austin Energy personnel's ability to access and maintain current and proposed electric facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(4). This includes vehicle and equipment access to transformers, poles, transmission structures, and other AE infrastructure. The site layout plan does not show dedicated access routes or confirm that adequate turning radii and passage widths are maintained for AE service vehicles (typically 24-foot wide vehicles). The absence of documented access provisions represents a deficiency.
findings.comment: Electric facility access routes not demonstrated on site plan. Provide documentation on the Site Plan showing clear vehicle access routes to all Austin Energy facilities (transformers, transmission structures, poles, vaults) with dimensions confirming adequate clearance for 24-foot wide AE service vehicles and equipment.

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformers and electrical equipment placement and routing. However, the blocks.md and guide.md for Sheet 21 do not document specific service voltage (e.g., 120/240V, 208V/120V three-phase, 480V) or service characteristics (single-phase vs. three-phase, service amperage, transformer capacity in kVA) with documentation of AE Design determination and approval. The preliminary design shows equipment placement but does not include voltage and capacity specifications with AE Design approval letters or correspondence.
findings.reasoning: Plans showing service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) require documentation of AE Design determination and approval per UCM § 1.3.2. Applicants cannot self-determine service specifications; these are determined and approved by AE Design based on load analysis and available infrastructure. If service specifications are shown on the plans without AE Design approval documentation, or if they are not shown at all, this is a deficiency. Evidence of AE Design approval must accompany any service specifications shown on plans.
findings.comment: Service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) not shown with Austin Energy Design approval documentation. Either remove service specifications from the plans, or provide an AE Design approval letter confirming the voltage, phases, service size, and transformer capacity shown are available and approved for this location.

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformers and equipment on the plan. From the available documentation, it appears there may be multiple transformer locations shown, but the specific number of service points (service drops from transformers) and whether multiple voltage levels are proposed cannot be definitively determined from the blocks.md review. No documentation of AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval for multiple points of service or multiple voltages was located.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 establishes a default rule of one point of service at one service voltage to a single building on a single lot. Exceptions require AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval. If the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows multiple points of service (multiple service drops to different buildings or multiple voltage levels), documentation of the exception approval is required. Without clarity on whether multiple service points are proposed, or without approval documentation if they are, this requirement cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Multiple points of service or multiple voltages not verified. Confirm whether the project requires one or multiple points of service and one or multiple service voltages. If multiple points of service or voltages are proposed, provide AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval letter for the exception to the one-point-of-service rule.

findings.observation: The Consolidated Site Plan Application (Property Attributes section) shows the project is NOT participating in affordable housing programs. The checkbox for S.M.A.R.T. Housing is marked 'No', and no affordable housing certification letter or Housing and Planning Department documentation is provided. Therefore, no line extension fee waiver is being claimed.
findings.reasoning: This item is only applicable if the applicant claims an affordable housing line extension fee waiver under the S.M.A.R.T. Housing Program. Since the project explicitly does not include affordable housing and is not claiming a waiver, this item is not applicable to this project.
findings.comment: Not applicable - project does not claim affordable housing line extension fee waiver.
